caption: The wire of a garden fence is plucked, and the wire blurs and hums along its span before settling.

sa.check: A garden fence with a wire strand.
The wire blurs along its span.
The wire settles to a sharp line.
One wire is plucked; the other strands are left alone.
The order is pluck, blur, settle.

pc.expect: The wire is sharp and still until the fingers pull it; the blur begins at the pluck and only then; the other wires stay sharp.
pc.fail: The wire is already blurred before the hand reaches it; or blurs while the hand is well away; or the hand plucks and the wire stays a sharp line; or a different wire blurs from the one plucked.

pc.expect: The blur is widest right after the release and narrows steadily until the wire is sharp; it does not widen again.
pc.fail: The blur widens after it has begun to narrow; or holds the same width for the whole clip; or the wire goes sharp and blurs again with nothing touching it.

pc.expect: The wire vibrates between its fixed posts: the blur lies between the posts, widest around the plucked point, and the wire stays attached.
pc.fail: The wire pulls free of a post; or the blur is at the posts and absent at the plucked point; or the wire sags into a loop and hangs slack; or a post leans with the pluck.

pc.expect: When a hand closes on the vibrating wire the blur stops at once and the whole wire is sharp.
pc.fail: The wire keeps blurring through and beyond the gripping hand; or the span stays blurred for the rest of the clip while the hand holds it; or the wire starts blurring again after the hand lets go with no new pluck.
pc.precondition: A hand grips the wire while it is still blurred.

pc.expect: The fence keeps its wires and posts; the plucked wire stays one strand and passes through nothing.
pc.fail: Wires appear or vanish; or the wire passes through the hand or a post; or the wire splits into two strands; or a post vanishes.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The wire's colour, the posts and the garden behind stay the same.
pc.fail: The wire changes colour; or the posts change spacing between frames; or the plants behind change.

note: The hum is inaudible and is not judged. The caption does not say the wire is gripped; P4 applies only if a hand is seen closing on it.
